ITW.thesis_one_line: A best-in-class maker of industrial components and equipment with steady margins and buybacks, but its share price already assumes slightly more growth than the evidence supports.
kill_criteria: Organic revenue growth below 1.0% for two consecutive quarters (Q2-26: +4.5%).
Full-year GAAP EPS guidance midpoint cut below $11.00 (Q2-26 midpoint: $11.45).
Total debt/EBITDA above 2.5x in the 10-Q MD&A "Total Debt to EBITDA" table (Jun-26: 2.0x).
Consolidated operating margin below 25.0% in two consecutive quarters (Q2-26: 26.7%).
TTM free cash flow below 90% of TTM net income at year-end 2026 (TTM to Jun-26: 91%).
key_adverse_facts: Q2-26 organic growth +4.5% is carried by Welding +13.9% and Test & Measurement/Electronics +10.0%; Automotive OEM -0.4% and Food Equipment 0.0%.
Price/cost timing lags diluted margin; Specialty Products margin -110 bps and Welding -70 bps in Q2-26.

Debt rose to $9,694M consolidated carrying value (commercial paper $2.1bn) and a $1.5bn 4.650% note due 2029 was issued 13 Aug 2026 (8-K 0001193125-26-349149); equity only $2,895M after $28.0bn treasury stock.
Reverse DCF implies 7.6% FCF growth vs base 7.0%.
data_conflicts: d4 FCF yield 3.1% (Yahoo FCF $2,433M) vs 3.7% on filing TTM FCF $2,921M.
b1 ROE 98th percentile is a buyback/leverage artefact (equity $2,895M).
ITW.confidence_in_thesis: high on business quality (four straight guidance raises or narrowings, 91% FCF/NI); medium on returns given valuation

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Corrected by verification DV23 (2026-10-08): reverse DCF at the programme cost of equity 9.30% (5.17% + Blume beta 0.998 x 4.14%) on FCF after SBC ($2.84bn), terminal 3%, implies about 9.9% ten-year FCF growth vs my 7.0% base (above; base value about $221). The original 8.5% and FCF before SBC implied 7.6%.

ITW.scenario_basis: FY26 GAAP EPS midpoint $11.45; EPS growth bear 3%/base 7.5%/bull 10% to exit NTM EPS at Sep-2029 (3.5 years compounding); exit P/E 17x/21x/24x vs 22.6x now; dividend $6.88 rising, ~2.5% yield.

LYB.thesis_one_line: A commodity plastics and chemicals maker enjoying a temporary war-driven profit spike; cash flow is weak, the dividend was halved, and the price already reflects normal profits.
kill_criteria: Net debt/TTM EBITDA excluding identified items above 3.5x at any quarter-end (Jun-26: 2.6x).
Trailing-four-quarter free cash flow (OCF less capex) negative at December 2026 year-end (Jun-26 TTM ~$1.58bn positive; H1-26 negative).
Quarterly dividend cut below $0.69 per share.
EBITDA excluding identified items below $600M in any quarter of H2-26 or H1-27 (Q1-26: $615M).
Loss of investment-grade credit rating by any of S&P, Moody's, Fitch.
key_adverse_facts: Q2-26 adjusted EPS $4.30 vs $0.49 in Q1-26 driven by Middle East supply disruption; management says recovery 'likely extending into 2027'.
Dividend cut 50% to $0.69 per quarter in February 2026 (10-K).
H1-26 FCF -$56M (OCF $483M, capex $539M) plus $310M cash paid into disposed European businesses; FY25 FCF $384M vs $1.76bn dividends.
Consolidated total debt $12,910M; net debt/TTM EBITDA ex-items 2.6x (4.0x on FY25).
Q2-26 GAAP includes $734M loss on sale of European assets; average earnings surprise -15% over 8 quarters (d4).
data_conflicts: d4 FY26 consensus EPS $9.04 vs FY27 $6.31: FY26 is war-inflated.
d4 fcf_yield 6.5% uses TTM FCF flattered by H2-25 working-capital release; Yahoo total debt $14.3bn includes leases vs $12,910M filing total debt.
LYB.confidence_in_thesis: low: outcomes depend on commodity spreads and Middle East supply recovery

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. On normalised FCF of $1.3bn at 10%/3% the price implies 2.8% growth (originally stated ~3.5%); with SBC (~$130M a year) deducted the base is ~$1.17bn and the implied growth 4.2% vs base 3.0%: above, no margin of safety. [DV27 2026-10-08: restated]

LYB.scenario_basis: Mid-cycle adjusted EPS bear $2.50 at 14x / base $5.25 at 11x / bull $8.00 at 12x vs $58.14; dividend $2.76 (4.7%) in base and bull, cut to ~$1.40 in bear.

FTV.thesis_one_line: A simplified maker of test tools, safety sensors and hospital products growing about 6%, turning profits into cash and buying back shares at a roughly 6% free-cash-flow yield.
kill_criteria: Core revenue growth below 2.0% for two consecutive quarters (Q2-26: 6.7%).
FY26 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint cut below $2.90 (Q2-26 midpoint: $3.00).
Net debt/adjusted EBITDA above 3.25x (10-Q covenant limit 3.75x; now ~2.4x).
TTM free cash flow below $900M (Q2-26 TTM $1,044M).
AHS segment adjusted EBITDA margin below 24.0% in any quarter (Q2-26: 26.1%).
key_adverse_facts: Reservation: only four quarters of new-Fortive track record since the 28 Jun 2025 Ralliant spin; adjusted EPS growth is helped by ~11% share shrink over four quarters.
GAAP vs adjusted gap large: Q2-26 $0.51 vs $0.74; H1-26 amortization $184.7M excluded.
Q2-26 GAAP margin includes +40 bps from IEEPA tariff refunds; Q1-26 growth had ~150 bps selling-day help.
AHS adjusted EBITDA margin 26.1% (-80 bps) in Q2-26.
Long-term debt $3,509.3M consolidated (incl. commercial paper) up $303M in H1-26 while $700M was repurchased.
data_conflicts: b1 Sentiment 10th percentile and ROE are distorted by the Ralliant spin (continuing vs total operations).
d4 FCF yield 5.5% (Yahoo FCF $939M) vs 6.1% on filing TTM FCF $1,044M.
FTV.confidence_in_thesis: medium: cash yield and valuation are solid, but the record is short and includes one-offs

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists. Restated 2026-10-10 (DV18) on the programme basis: Ke 9.24% (5.17% + 0.982 x 4.14%), equity value $17.1bn, FCF after SBC $950M: implied 10-year FCF growth is 4.1%/yr (original 1.3% at 8.5%, 2.4% SBC-adjusted) vs the 5.5% base; still below but a much thinner margin (the 5.5% path is worth 1.11x market value).

FTV.scenario_basis: FY26 adjusted EPS midpoint $3.00; adjusted EPS growth 3%/9%/12% to 3.5 years; exit P/E 15x/18x/20x vs 17.6x NTM now; dividend $0.28 (0.5%).
